evidence.evidence_paraphrase: Au@Ag core-shell nanoparticles are prepared and combined with MMT; the substrate is characterized and optimized, but no paired solution-versus-dried comparison is described.

R6G solutions are uniformly mixed with the substrate, drop-cast onto glass slides, air-dried, and then analyzed by SERS; the study reports concentration response and spatial RSD for this dried configuration.

For thiram, equal volumes of analyte solution and MMT/Au@Ag nanoparticles are mixed and applied to apple skin for SERS analysis, with concentration calibration and reproducibility reported rather than a solution-to-dried comparison.

assessments.scientific_rationale: The paper uses Au@Ag core-shell nanoparticles with analytes mixed into the substrate and then drop-cast and air-dried before SERS measurement. However, it does not establish the frozen paired solution-to-dried relation because the same preparation is not measured in both contexts and no context-dependent change in normalized peak intensities or peak profile is reported.

evidence.evidence_paraphrase: The reported material is an MMT-supported Au@Ag core-shell nanoparticle substrate, with UV irradiation time and MMT-to-particle mixing ratio optimized; no polymer-defined Ag bridge or controlled gap variation is examined.
The study reports SERS intensity, concentration calibration, and spatial uniformity for R6G and thiram, without testing a directional response to controlled nanogap dimensions.

assessments.scientific_rationale: The paper contains Au@Ag core-shell nanoparticles and reports SERS enhancement, but it does not study the polymer-separated Ag-bridge architecture or controlled variation of an inner/outer Ag gap. It therefore does not support the architecture-specific directional gap-size relation.
